artworks.title: The Mutilation of Uranus by Saturn
artworks.description: Ceiling painting from the Sala degli Elementi of the Palazzo Vecchio in Florence, rendering Hesiod's pivotal cosmogonic act: Cronus unmans his father Uranus with the adamantine sickle Gaia forged, and from the blood and foam the Erinyes, Giants and Aphrodite will spring. The image anchors the succession myth that opens the Theogony and the whole cosmic cycle shelf.

artworks.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
artworks.description: Commissioned for the Torre de la Parada, Rubens depicts Cronus tearing into an infant son beneath his scythe — the devouring that Hesiod places between the castration of Uranus and the birth of Zeus. The painting visualizes the second age of the cosmos, when Rhea would save the youngest child with a stone wrapped in swaddling clothes.

artworks.title: Chaos
artworks.description: Watts's Tate allegory of the first gap: elemental titans heave from fire and vapour — Hesiod's Chaos before Earth and sky take form.

artworks.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
artworks.description: Goya's Black Painting returns Cronus' appetite as modern nightmare — the cosmogonic devouring stripped of Olympus' polish.

artworks.title: The Creation of the World (Orbis fabrica)
artworks.description: Tempesta's Metamorphoses plate opens with earth, sea and sky parting from formless Chaos — Ovid's cosmogony as the first metamorphosis of all.
